_about: Postflop behavior by hand class, used to narrow ranges and to predict how opponents respond to your bets. Classes: setPlus (sets, trips, straights, flushes and better that use a hole card), twoPair, overpair, topPairGood (kicker T or better), topPairWeak, middlePair, weakPair, strongDraw (flush draw or open-ender), weakDraw (gutshot or two overcards), air. Values describe a low-stakes regular; profiles.json scales them for each opponent style.

firstToAct._about: Share of each class that bets small (up to half pot) or big (more than half pot) when first to act or checked to. The rest checks.

facingBet._about: Chance to continue facing a bet of size f (bet divided by the pot before the bet): base - slope * f, clipped to 0..1. Past maxSize (an overbet), the line stops and the chance instead shrinks by (maxSize / f) ^ (overbetDecay * slope): hands that barely mind bet size (sets, overpairs, good top pairs) keep calling a huge overbet or shove at nearly the same rate, while weak pairs, draws and air give up. 'raise' is the share of continuing hands that raise; the rest call. 'defend' is a floor for the whole range: it keeps at least this share of the minimum defense frequency 1 / (1 + f), plus the style's continueAdd. When the table would fold more than that (a range that checked holds a lot of air and weak pairs), every class's continue chance grows by the same factor, at most maxBoost times its own and never past always, until the range reaches the floor. Pairs and draws take up the extra defense while air keeps folding, so a polarized range of strong hands and air can stay short of the floor. Without it, betting any two cards would earn a profit.

realization._about: Share of raw equity a hand is expected to realize before the river: the position value times the hand-class factor (draws and nutted hands realize more, weak pairs and air less). On the river, or once all-in, equity is realized fully.

leadIntoAggressor._about: First to act on a street when the opponent was the last aggressor (for example the big blind on the flop after calling an open). Most hands check to the raiser; these are the shares that lead small or big instead.

laterStreets._about: Value a hand that is ahead adds on the streets still to come when the hand does not end now. Each later street gets one bet of betSize times the pot (capped by the stacks). Against each opponent hand the hero beats more often than not, the hero wins (2 * equity - 1) of those bets times the chance that hand calls a bet of that size (facingBet). Hands that are behind are assumed to give up rather than pay off, so they add nothing.

facingRaise._about: Multiplier on the continue chance when the player had bet and is now facing a raise. Raises are stronger than bets, so one-pair hands give up somewhat more often, but players at these stakes rarely fold a pair to a single raise. 'defend' works as under facingBet, for a range that bet and is raised: a range of small bets holds many bluffs and weak pairs, and without the floor any raise would be a profitable bluff.

textures._about: Multipliers on the class tables by board texture (src/engine/postflop/texture.ts). betSmall and betBig scale how often each class bets small or big, first to act and when leading into the last aggressor; continue scales how often it continues facing a bet, before the defense floor. 'about' is the line the feedback shows. A texture with imported solver spots uses the solver's figures for the classes those spots cover, in place of the multiplier. These are estimates for a low-stakes regular, not solver output.

dryHigh.about: On a dry ace- or king-high board the preflop raiser has most of the strong hands, so players bet small and often, even with nothing, and weak pairs call more readily since few cards change much.

dryLow.about: On a dry queen-high or lower board ranges are closer, so players bet a little less big, and overcards keep calling more since many turns give them a pair.

wet.about: On a connected or two-tone board strong hands and draws bet bigger to charge the draws, players make fewer small bets, and weak pairs and air fold more to a bet while draws continue more.

paired.about: On a paired board few hands improve, so players bet small more often and big less often, and small pairs hold up better against a bet.

monotone.about: With three cards of a suit out, one-pair hands bet much less and fold more to a bet, while flushes and flush draws bet and continue more.
